summary: Hansa Teutonica is a lean, cutthroat network-building game where you race to claim trade routes with only two actions per turn, and can bump rival pieces off routes to steal their position. It rewards efficient upgrading of personal abilities as much as raw map presence.
praised: high replayability with multiple viable strategies
criticised: can feel mean when pieces get bumped back to supply
some upkeep tracking bonuses slows new players

interaction.kind: Displacing opponents' merchants off contested trade routes to complete your own
interaction.detail: Completing a route means kicking a rival's piece back to their supply (with a small compensation), so a large share of decisions are made specifically to deny or disrupt an opponent's network. The trade-route board is entirely shared, and skill development is one of the few things that stays personal.
interaction.said: Widely described as "mean," "take-that for a euro," and known for the mechanic where you physically bump opponents' pieces off trade routes — reviewers regularly flag it as unusually aggressive for its genre

scoring.how_you_win: With only two actions per turn, complete trade routes and advance ability tracks to bank points continuously, then add end-game bonus tiles when someone triggers the end; highest total wins.

theme.said: widely called one of the most abstract, dry euros around — 'the trade routes could be anything', 'pure network optimization with a Hansa skin', 'no theme at all really'
theme.why: displacing another player's marker along a route and choosing between adding a bonus die or upgrading a personal ability track is pure abstract optimization that has nothing to do with Hanseatic trade specifically

style.why: Player pieces get displaced instead of destroyed, powers are symmetric, and outcomes hinge on efficient route-building rather than luck.
